summary: Over the 14-day analysis period, telemetry demonstrates exceptionally high glycemic control with a Time-in-Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, 0.0% Time-Below-Range (<70 mg/dL), and a low glucose coefficient of variation of 12.9%. Core profile parameters (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA) and AAPS automation settings are well-calibrated. Transient postprandial rises up to 188 mg/dL during Weekend Brunch resolve cleanly by 240 minutes without postprandial hypoglycemia. Minor timing adjustments to meal prebolus execution can further flatten postprandial peaks without altering underlying insulin settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Continuous glucose monitoring data spans 14 complete days with 100% coverage (1,345 entries, 0 gaps over 15 minutes). Telemetry, active profile parameters, and meal strategy records are fully populated and consistent.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid entries across 14 days with 0 gaps >15m; complete AAPS active profile segments; declared meal strategies for breakfast and brunch.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Physical activity intensity and detailed meal macronutrient composition (beyond declared high-fat context) are not recorded in sensor logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic variability is exceptionally low with zero clinical hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) across the entire 14-day evaluation window. Isolated overnight nadirs reached 70-71 mg/dL without requiring rescue carbohydrates.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall mean glucose 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, CV 12.9%, TBR (<70 mg/dL) 0.0%, TAR (>180 mg/dL) 0.3%. High glucose extreme was 188.0 mg/dL on 3 days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Context surrounding isolated overnight glucose nadirs (e.g., unlogged exercise or late-day physical activity).

analysis_steps.findings: Basal rates hold glucose flat and within target range during all fasting and overnight windows (00:00-06:00 local average 102.3-107.5 mg/dL). Active target segments (90-115 mg/dL) are safe and achievable.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local hourly mean glucose remains between 102.3 and 107.5 mg/dL with 100% TIR. Non-meal daytime intervals stay stable between 106.2 and 113.5 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Possible minor active insulin carryover (IOB) from late-evening dinners during the early sleep window.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios across all time segments adequately cover meal carbs, returning glucose to baseline by 240-360 minutes post-meal. ISF (40-48 mg/dL/U) and DIA (5.5 h) allow stable decay without stacking or late hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows show 240-minute glucose changes relative to start of -2 to +8 mg/dL for weekday breakfasts and -11 to +1 mg/dL for weekend brunches.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact precision of carbohydrate counting and individual variations in daily physical activity.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM algorithm settings are active and functioning safely. Micro-boluses effectively assist in dampening postprandial spikes without over-delivering insulin or causing late postprandial turns.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true; smb_interval_minutes=3, max_smb_basal_minutes=45, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30; 0% TBR across 14 days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Raw telemetry exports leave specific UI activation toggle flags (smb_always_enabled, etc.) unpopulated (null).

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (max basal 2.4 U/h, max IOB 8.0 U) provide sufficient operational room for automated corrections while maintaining strong protection against insulin stacking. Sensitivity adjustments are stable.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour (2.4 U/h) is ~2.3x highest basal segment (1.05 U/h); max_iob_units (8.0 U) safely accommodates largest meal boluses (5.8 U) plus SMB headroom.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens specific UI toggle flags are unpopulated (null) in Nightscout export logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal strategies successfully maintain 99.7% TIR. Weekday Breakfast (20m prebolus, 70% immediate) results in moderate peak (157-167 mg/dL). Weekend Brunch (10m prebolus, 60% immediate) peaks higher (188 mg/dL) due to high-fat mixed meal absorption delay.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows show 120m glucose rise of +33 to +57 mg/dL for breakfast and +62 to +70 mg/dL for brunch, both settling cleanly to baseline by 240 minutes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact timestamp of first food bite relative to bolus execution in daily routine.

analysis_steps.findings: The declared Weekend Brunch strategy using 20g eCarbs (120m duration, 15m start offset) correctly accounts for extended fat/protein absorption. The high 120m peak (188 mg/dL) is driven by bolus timing rather than insufficient extended insulin.
analysis_steps.evidence: Postprandial curve peaks at 120m (188 mg/dL) and descends smoothly to 115 mg/dL at 240m and 111 mg/dL at 360m under combined eCarb and UAM delivery.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unmeasured variance in fat and protein content across different brunch meals.

analysis_steps.findings: All findings across profile, automation, and meal strategies are harmonious and consistent. No profile parameter adjustments are required. The primary actionable finding is optimizing Weekend Brunch prebolus timing to lower the 120m peak.
analysis_steps.evidence: 100% concordance between high TIR (99.7%), flat overnight basal trends, complete 4-hour meal recovery, and safe AAPS automation limits.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None; telemetry data is sufficient to confirm profile stability and synthesize safe recommendations.

strengths: Exceptional 99.7% Time-in-Range (70-180 mg/dL) across 14 consecutive days of continuous monitoring.
Zero clinical hypoglycemia (0.0% Time-Below-Range <70 mg/dL) and low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%).
Basal profile rates perfectly maintain glucose stability during overnight and fasting daytime windows.
AAPS automation parameters (SMB, UAM, safety limits) operate safely without compensating for underlying profile errors.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose peaks reach up to 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes following high-fat mixed Weekend Brunches.

recommendations.title: Optimize Weekend Brunch Prebolus Timing
recommendations.description: Weekend Brunch currently uses a 10-minute prebolus, resulting in a 120-minute postprandial rise to 188 mg/dL before returning to 115 mg/dL by 240 minutes. Extending the prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes can help reduce this early absorption peak while preserving the current 60% immediate / 20g eCarb distribution.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Active basal rates, targets, CR, ISF, and DIA achieve 99.7% Time-in-Range and 0.0% Time-Below-Range with flat overnight trends. Profile parameters are optimal and require no changes.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Evaluate postprandial peak during Weekend Brunch after testing a 15-20 minute prebolus timing.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current profile basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA settings unchanged.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain a 15-20 minute prebolus with a 70% immediate bolus for fast carbohydrates (e.g. Weekday Breakfast). For higher-fat/mixed meals (e.g. Weekend Brunch), utilize a 15-20 minute prebolus with a 60% immediate bolus and 20g eCarbs over 120 minutes, relying on AAPS SMB/UAM automation to absorb residual delayed rises safely.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Current bolus splits and eCarb strategies achieve an outstanding 99.7% TIR with zero hypoglycemia. Extending prebolus timing slightly for high-fat brunches will reduce the 120-minute 188 mg/dL peak without introducing early hypoglycemia risk.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether increasing the Weekend Brunch prebolus from 10 to 15-20 minutes reduces the 2-hour peak below 160 mg/dL without causing glucose to drop below 90 mg/dL in the first 60 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Maintain 20 minute prebolus, 70% immediate bolus, no eCarbs.
exceptions.rationale: Fast carbs (coffee and bread) are well-managed by this split, returning to baseline by 240 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Extend prebolus timing from 10 to 15-20 minutes while retaining 60% immediate bolus and 20g eCarbs over 120 minutes (15 min offset).
exceptions.rationale: Higher-fat mixed meals cause a delayed rise peaking at 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes; slightly earlier bolus delivery better matches early carbohydrate absorption.

implementation_steps: Maintain all current AAPS profile parameters (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA, targets) as configured.
Verify in the AAPS smartphone UI that SMB activation triggers and Autosens settings match your preferred configuration (since export flags were null).
For the next Weekend Brunch, test extending prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15 minutes before eating.
Monitor glucose during the first 2 hours post-brunch to confirm that the peak is reduced and early glucose remains above 90 mg/dL.
If 15 minutes is well tolerated and glucose stays stable, test a 20-minute prebolus for future mixed brunches.
education: Prebolus timing controls the alignment between insulin onset and carbohydrate absorption. For high-fat/high-protein meals, rapid-acting insulin given too late can lag behind fast carbs before fat slows absorption, creating a temporary peak followed by a late drop.

Extended carbohydrates (eCarbs) in AAPS simulate gradual carbohydrate absorption, allowing SMB micro-boluses to be delivered incrementally rather than all at once, which prevents early postprandial hypoglycemia during mixed meals.
safety_notes: This analysis is for decision-support and educational review only. Independent verification is required prior to making any treatment changes.
Always evaluate proposed behavioral or parameter changes one at a time and monitor blood glucose closely following any adjustment.
Consult with your professional healthcare team or endocrinologist before modifying insulin dosing strategies or algorithm settings.
